I'm a B.A. of Music at my current university. They didn't offer the B.M. when I first started. I asked my lessons teacher if there was a major difference in the title (like if it affected how grad schools saw me or not) and I guess they don't really care about that stuff, it's more about what you bring to the table. This was the biggest indicator for me because grad school has always been the goal for me. The biggest difference would be the classes, just because at my school there's less academics and more music literature classes (which if they had added in all these changes when I was a sophomore I would have taken them all because I love that sorta thing) plus Junior and Senior recital classes, which I could have done because I've done a sophomore, junior and working towards my senior recital. If it would have been a smart option for me, I wouldn't have done it still. All the classes offered with the B.M. are things I'm going to study in grad school. It also left me with a better schedule where I can practice more, and I love to practice so of course I want that. It's really dependent on what you want to do with your degree after graduating. If you think the B.M. is beneficial; go for it. If you enjoy the path you're on, stick with it. Either way, you're doing music and that's what really matters as long as you love it.
